headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: plano has broad network egress and API calls, while the zoomcamp profile is docs-only and non-runnable, so other risks are mostly absent or low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default communication channel is documented between data-engineering-zoomcamp and plano. A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; B has API calls and broad egress, but nothing shows it ingests A’s outputs by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A’s text into B’s prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted course content into plano prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any shared inputs.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization before B consumes A-derived text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is docs-only and non-runnable, so it does not itself expose runtime data. B has broad network egress and calls an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, so if any shared workspace or copied material contains sensitive data, B can transmit it off-box. The pairwise leakage risk exists in default B behavior, but A contributes no sensitive runtime surface.
conditions: IF A-derived files containing sensitive material are placed into B’s config or prompt inputs, leakage becomes possible.
IF B is pointed at a third-party chat endpoint, transmitted context leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any shared files.
Review B’s endpoint target before use.
Use a local-only endpoint for B if available.
requires-engineering: add redaction before outbound API calls.
requires-engineering: isolate A and B into separate storage roots.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write surfaces and is non-runnable, while B cannot spawn subprocesses and only exposes API calls plus a config file. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources such as shared filesystem writes or git state, so capability conflict is limited to unusual operator-created overlap.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same writable directory, write conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator grants B additional filesystem or git write permissions, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep separate config directories.
Avoid sharing a mutable workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks for any shared state.
requires-engineering: restrict B to read-only access where possible.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course repository and not a runnable agent, so it does not generate operational facts for B to act on by default. B is a travel-planning gateway that can route API calls, but there is no documented pipeline where B treats A’s output as authoritative. The cascade pathway is therefore weak and mostly manual.
conditions: IF an operator feeds A-generated text into B without review, B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to auto-act on upstream text, cascade risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before B uses A-derived content.
Label A outputs as untrusted.
requires-engineering: add validation checks before B forwards content.
requires-engineering: separate generation from action-taking steps.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, and B’s documented data classes are agentic signals, traces, metrics, and logs. There is no shown PHI, EU PII, residency constraint, or retention-policy conflict between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated personal data, a separate compliance review is needed.
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data is routed through either agent.
Document retention settings for B.
requires-engineering: add data-class tagging to shared workflows.
requires-engineering: enforce residency controls if regulated data is introduced.
